claims.text: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 can be fabricated by LPBF through in-situ alloying of mixed elemental powders with complete powder fusion.
NbMoTaW can be formed as a single BCC solid solution by laser powder-bed processing.
The as-built BCC solid solution in the proposed alloys is metastable.
LPBF produces a fine cellular or dendritic microstructure in these alloys.
Solution annealing followed by stepwise aging will generate coherent B2 nanoprecipitates in the target W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V or Nb-Mo-Ta-W alloys.
Aging at 600-900 °C can produce B2 precipitates smaller than approximately 10-20 nm.
The desired inverted microstructure consists of discrete B2 precipitates dispersed in a continuous BCC matrix.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that could initiate cracks.
The coherent precipitates increase strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Strengthening occurs through precipitate shearing or Orowan bypass.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves room-temperature ductility while retaining high yield strength.
The inverted coherent-precipitate microstructure mitigates brittleness caused specifically by interstitial impurities.
The optimized target alloy will have yield strength above 1.0 GPa at 800 °C.
The optimized target alloy will exhibit more than approximately 10-15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
The alloy will retain structural integrity at 800-900 °C because the coherent B2 precipitates are thermally stable.
As-built single-phase LPBF refractory HEAs typically have tensile ductility below 5%.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix causes poor room-temperature ductility in two-phase refractory HEAs.
The high melting points of refractory HEAs make conventional processing difficult, while laser additive manufacturing is feasible.
Excessive aging will coarsen the precipitates, destroy coherency, and return the alloy to a brittle state.
The strategy will not transfer to FCC refractory HEAs or to alloys in which B2 precipitates are incoherent or form a continuous network.

contradictions.description: The proposed as-built state is repeatedly described as a single-phase BCC solid solution, but the baseline and mechanism also attribute its brittleness to a continuous ordered B2 phase. A genuinely single-phase disordered BCC state cannot simultaneously contain a continuous B2 phase; the text does not distinguish the target as-built alloy from other two-phase RHEAs.
